title: The Secret to Self-Control
coreMove: Reduce exposure to tempting cues so discipline happens upstream of the urge.
sourcePressure: What looks like self-control often reflects encountering tempting cues less often rather than winning constant direct fights against them.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating self-control as heroic resistance instead of fewer cue collisions.

hook: starting with a definition of self-control
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a casino security analyst routing employees away from slot-floor shortcuts
exampleSpecs.audience: a manager whose staff gamble after shifts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether fewer cue encounters beats daily resistance
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: badge logs show the employees who used the back corridor stopped making after-shift bets
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a staff badge reader beside a service corridor door

exampleSpecs.domain: a night baker storing sample pastries in sealed crates outside the prep line
exampleSpecs.audience: a baker who grazes through every overnight shift
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether removing aroma and sight reduces the fight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she wheels the sealed crate into the walk-in before glazing starts and notices the urge never spikes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sealed pastry crate sliding into a walk-in shelf

exampleSpecs.domain: a paramedic deleting the trauma-forum shortcut from the station tablet
exampleSpecs.audience: a medic who doomscrolls between calls
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether less exposure protects recovery time
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he reaches for the old shortcut after a hard call and finds only the dispatch checklist
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a station tablet locked to a dispatch screen

exampleSpecs.domain: a rare-book dealer moving auction alerts to a separate offline laptop
exampleSpecs.audience: a collector who overspends during late auctions
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether frictionless exposure was the real self-control problem
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the alert does not appear on the pricing computer, so the bid window passes without a battle
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an auction catalog closed beside a pricing monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: a college swimmer choosing a route that bypasses the vending alcove
exampleSpecs.audience: an athlete trying to stop late candy runs
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether changing the hallway removes the cue before craving appears
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she exits through the pool-deck stairwell and realizes no decision happened at all
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet footprints leading toward a pool-deck stairwell

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance editor keeping game controllers in a locked equipment cabinet during deadline week
exampleSpecs.audience: a self-employed worker who loses evenings to short breaks
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether making the cue absent matters more than promising restraint
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he tells his roommate where the key is and the 9 p.m. trigger ends at an empty shelf
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an empty TV shelf with only a remote tray

skillTargets: move discipline upstream by removing cues
distinguish avoidance design from weak character
choose exposure changes over heroic resistance

tryThisNowSpec: Remove one tempting cue from a place you pass daily, or change the route so you do not meet it today.
